newsitem.title: FRANCE: French AFB bank group challenges CIC sale.
newsitem.headline: French AFB bank group challenges CIC sale.

text.p: The French AFB banks association said on Wednesday that a takeover of CIC bank by savings bank grouping Caisses d'Epargne would be open to challenge on the grounds that it would not amount to a privatisation.
The government intends to sell 67 percent of CIC, which is a unit of state insurer GAN.

"This operation should not and cannot happen," AFB head Patrice Cahart told reporters at a routine monthly briefing. "I believe the public authorities will hesitate before getting involved in a legally dubious operation."
Cahart said the CIC sale had to be to the private sector to be considered a privatisation.

Former finance minister Pierre Beregovoy had clearly stated in a parliamentary debate on Caisses d'Epargne statutes in the past that the savings bank grouping did not have private law statutes, he said.

"You can't transfer it (CIC) to anything other than the private sector," he said, also highlighting that the Caisses grouping was 40 percent-controlled by the state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations.
The Caisse d'Epargne was likely to say on September 18, when its board meets to decide whether it was making an offer for CIC, Cahart added.
"It would be shocking if the Caisses d'Epargne buys CIC from the state with the state's money," Cahart said.

He said a monopoly on distribution of the popular pass-book Livret A savings account backed by the state had allowed the mutual Caisses d'Epargne group to build up "what are misleadingly called shareholder funds".

The savings bank group had been benefited for decades from a relatively hefty remuneration from the Caisse des Depots for distributing this Livret A product, Cahart said, noting that the AFB banks were proposing to do the same job cheaper.
Among AFB member banks, Societe Generale is the only one so far to declare itself in the running for CIC.
